summary: Phase 3 Pipeline Persistence passes security and data handling review. convex/pipelines.ts is fully deleted, removing all placeholder exports and 'stub-id' literals. No api.pipelines.* references remain in production code. All 18 tests (12 pivot route + 4 convex inversion + 2 regression) pass, typecheck is clean. Route handlers delegate to real convex/pipelineRuns.* handlers with validated Convex ID inputs. No secrets, env vars, or sensitive data are exposed in API responses. No new attack surface introduced — the deletion of dead placeholder code is a net security improvement.
nonblocking_findings: No authentication/authorization on pipeline routes (pre-existing architectural pattern across all pivot routes, not a Phase 3 regression)
Trigger route body is parsed but not validated against a schema (pre-existing pattern; other routes use routeBody for Zod validation, not used here)
Error messages from runPipeline are returned directly to the client via badRequest (pre-existing pattern across pivot routes)
storeExecution uses 'unknown' as fallback taskId which will fail Convex v.id('tasks') validation — silently swallowed, no data persisted but execution still runs
Convex mutation errors in storeExecution/updateExecutionStatus are silently caught — partial persistence is possible (execution runs, records not written)
